description: RelaxSearch is a lightweight, demonstration-based search engine project built with Go and Elasticsearch.

summary.one_liner: RelaxSearch is a small demonstration search engine written in Go on top of Elasticsearch, with a web crawler that indexes pages and a REST API that searches them.
summary.what_it_does: The project has two components. RelaxEngine is a web scraper that runs on cron jobs, reads a list of seed URLs, crawls from them, and indexes the retrieved content into Elasticsearch. RelaxWeb is an API server exposing GET /search, which takes a keyword and returns matching indexed content. The search endpoint supports optional pagination (from, size with a default of 10), date filtering via dateRangeStart and dateRangeEnd, and content highlighting. Configuration for Elasticsearch connection and scraping parameters lives in .env and config files under each service. Docker Compose starts Elasticsearch, the crawler, and the API, which serves on port 7000.
use_cases: learn how a basic search engine works
crawl seed URLs and index page content
keyword search over scraped web pages
REST search API with pagination and date filters
how_to_run: Configure .env files for RelaxEngine and RelaxWeb with Elasticsearch credentials
notable: Two-part design: a cron-driven crawler (RelaxEngine) and a separate search API (RelaxWeb)
Full-text search with optional date-range filtering and highlighting
Single docker-compose command brings up Elasticsearch, crawler, and API
caveats: README says it is limited to demonstration use and suited to small to medium datasets
Error handling is acknowledged as needing improvement
Requires configuring Elasticsearch credentials in .env files before running
keywords: index web pages for keyword search
